alt: Head: the fine-tune cuts the panel's rule to 33% but does not erase the signal: a classifier on the same 20 scores still catches 84%. Qwen2.5-1.5B reads a true statement, 'The city of Kobe is not in China.', and its false twin, 'The city of Kobe is not in Japan.' A grid has three models as rows and two ways to read the same 20 probe scores as columns. Each cell shows a pile of 596 true and a pile of 596 false test statements, an alarm line that 1% of true statements cross, and the Kobe pair as two dots. Left column, the panel's rule: each probe is re-standardised on the checked model's own true statements, and the highest score is compared with one alarm line. Right column: a classifier on the same 20 scores, trained with true and false labels on the checked model. Original model: the panel's rule catches 99.5% of false statements and the classifier 99.8%; both flag the false Kobe statement. Fine-tuned against the plain panel (last post, outputs kept): the panel's rule catches 64% and the classifier 83% (28% if trained on the original model's labels); both flag the false Kobe statement. Fine-tuned against the re-standardising panel (this post, outputs kept): the panel's rule catches 33% and misses the false Kobe statement; the classifier still catches 84% (20% if trained on the original model's labels) and flags it. Note below: only with the fine-tuned model's labels; with the original model's, it catches 20%. Percentages pool 3 runs; piles and dots come from run 3 of 3 (this post) and run 1 of 3 (last post), and the Kobe verdicts hold in all 3 runs.
